Jaissle on injuries, responding to Coventry loss and Fernandez-Pardo

Figure caption,

By Josh Lobley
BBC Sport journalist

Published

15 October 2026

Newcastle United boss Matthias Jaissle has been speaking to the media before Saturday's Premier League game against Aston Villa at St James' Park (kick-off 17:30 BST).

Here are the key lines from his news conference:

Bazoumana Toure is doing    after coming off in Monday's defeat at Coventry and Jaissle hopes he can be available.

On managing the minutes of returning players Joelinton and Dan Burn:   too soon  different 

 Now, it's the process is to bring back him back slowly but surely, in a smart way, and not too much in a hurry. Hopefully, next week, he is about to train again with the group, at least partially and we then integrate him again step by step. 

 We know about his injury situation and history, but we're optimistic in the next few weeks we can bring him back step by step.  partially 

 It's never easy after conceding four goals to talk about the structure and what causes us the problems. Against Coventry, we made too many individual mistakes, you cannot talk about formation or technical approach. Even though we're a young squad, we need to learn fast. 

 Young lads coming to the Premier League for the first time need that adaptation time. I got advice that I should be patient at least half a year with them. Of course, you don't have the time in the Premier League so the development and adjustment needs to be as fast as possible. He's creating the chances and I think it's just a goal missing to give him the confidence back. He's an amazing player and he has so much potential.
